This session so far: three fixes pushed, one more merged into the branch and waiting to push, and one change rejected. Pond, the case that measures detection of a real bug, is still not detected, because most of what blocks it is Go call resolution.

**Pushed to origin/master:**
- `0c1c768ac`: the #3760 soundness fix. Bifrost had reported a real race as proven absent; a row now claims ordering, protection or absence only when every task context proves it. #3760 is closed.
- `4956032a8`: complete answers are now shared across the roots of one query. The cache is used (5,135 hits on ants) and saves about 137,000 budget entries. But ants' root 10 alone needs more than the freed budget, so its row count did not change.
- `dd3ed8370`: the benchmark comparison no longer counts a known remaining race on a fixed revision as a regression.

**Waiting to push:** the change that names unresolved calls on race rows and adds reviewed models for calls that don't synchronize with shared memory (`time.NewTicker`, `time.Now`, `errors.New`, and others). The full gates passed after the merge (6,834 crate tests, 3,453 suite tests, clean Clippy). One more master merge and Clippy run are going now; I'll push when it finishes.

**Not accepted:** a change meant to keep an access's exact location after its pointer is passed to unknown code. Pond's row stayed open, and it broke 7 Java and Ruby typestate and resource-lifecycle tests. It is kept at `5f60cdc93` in `/tmp/bifrost-wt-mustalias`, and the plan records why.

**What the new unresolved-call data shows (confirmed on pond, ants, cache2go and workerpool):**
- Most `UnresolvedTarget` reasons come from dispatch the analyzer can't resolve: 1,989 occurrences, against roughly 900 for all missing library models together.
- On pond, the blocking calls are:
  - a function defined in another file of the same package (`Eager()`);
  - calls through function values;
  - `idleTicker.Stop()`, which has a model but isn't matched to it, because the type returned by `time.NewTicker` isn't carried to the receiver;
  - an interface call;
  - `context.Done`, which needs a real context model, because cancellation does synchronize.

**Environment problems:**
- Child sessions can't build in their sandbox: mbx's socket isn't available there, so cargo stalls. Children now do only read-only work and experiments with prebuilt binaries, and I run the builds and gates.
- Your mbx cache deleted the first benchmark run's own build directory partway through. The rerun uses copied binaries and has finished 40 of 68 cases.

**Decision for you:** you said Go is in flight elsewhere. If that covers call resolution (cross-file functions, types returned by library calls, function values), it is the main thing between us and detecting pond's real bug, so I'm leaving it alone. If nobody owns it, it should probably be the next piece of work here.

Status: I've read the Go rollout notes, and I'm waiting for current master to build so I can see whether its Go resolution work has already changed pond's unresolved calls.

The Go call resolution I pointed to is already owned by the native Go resolution rollout. So the race work shouldn't take it on.

**Where it happens:** `../bifrost2` itself holds only Java work beyond master (11 commits on branch `2771`). The Go resolution work runs in detached `/mnt/optane` worktrees and lands on master in pieces. Recent examples:
- "Resolve Go external receiver calls from structured types" (`bc9ec425e`, today), which is the `idleTicker.Stop()` case on pond;
- "Resolve Go external package members from selected imports";
- "Derive Go variable types from runtime initializers".

Its plan (`.agents/docs/java-go-rollout-resume-2026-09-28.md`, dated 2026-09-30) shows it at step G3/G4, with more Go lanes still unmerged.

**What that means for race detection:** the plan says "No production routing for Java or Go yet". The new resolver is being built beside the old one and doesn't feed callers until a later cutover step. If the race analyzer's call targets come from that routing, pond's unresolved calls won't change until the cutover. That's likely, but I haven't confirmed it: I'm rebuilding current master now to see whether today's commits already changed pond's unresolved calls.

**The one thing to decide:** the race analyzer gets call targets from Go semantic lowering and its dispatch. The rollout plan lists which consumers it will reroute at cutover (definition, type, usages, calls, rename, graph), and that list doesn't clearly include semantic lowering's call targets. If it doesn't, the cutover won't fix race detection.

**My recommendation:** I don't duplicate any resolution work. Once the rebuild confirms what reaches race analysis today, I'll write a short issue asking the rollout to include semantic lowering's call targets in its cutover, with pond's unresolved call sites as test cases. Race work continues on what that lane doesn't cover: a `context` cancellation model, which synchronizes, and ants' root-10 cost.

I'll report the rebuild result when it finishes.
